requirements.description: The contact qualities the world requires. An empty list permits analytic primitive contact; any declared requirement selects the SDF field.

items.description: A contact quality authored by the world, independent of the engine implementation that supplies it.
items.title: WorldContactRequirement

contactSkin.description: The signed skin the solver keeps between a body and every surface (world units).

maxIterations.description: The relaxation iteration count per tick (above 8 is a solver pathology, not a choice).

maxSlopeDegrees.description: The steepest surface a body still counts as standing on. A contact whose normal leans further from the body's up axis than this pushes the body but never grounds it — the walkable-slope limit.

gradientProbe.description: The finite-difference step field contact samples the surface normal with, in world units; 0 takes the evaluator's own default. Meaningful only when a requirement selects field contact.

defaultHold.description: Whether a body's surface hold may take any solid surface by default. A placement's own WorldPlacementGrip overrides this for the colliders it compiles; the field lattice's own terrain, which no placement row owns, has only this. false (the default) holds nothing.

events.description: The bounded body-overlap event policy. ABSENT takes Default; author maxPairsPerBody: 0 to disable body-pair events while retaining ordinary world contact.

candidateBudget.description: The most sweep-and-prune candidates inspected for one body while discovering new overlaps. Must be at least MaxPairsPerBody.

maxPairsPerBody.description: The maximum retained overlap-event degree of one body; zero disables collision begin/end sensing.

beginBudget.description: The maximum collision-begin relationships admitted in one authority tick. Existing relationships and their ends are not delayed.

events.title: WorldCollisionEvents

bodyContacts.description: The bounded dynamic-body depenetration policy. ABSENT takes Default. This is independent of overlap events.

candidateBudget.description: The most sweep candidates inspected for one solid body. Must be at least MaxPairsPerBody.

maxPairsPerBody.description: The most body contacts incident to one body in a tick. It also sizes the rigid contact registry: a rigid body carries at most this many body contacts plus its surface contact, so no admitted contact is ever dropped for want of room.

rigidSubstepCeiling.description: The rigid solver's substeps per tick: each runs a velocity integration, a biased solve, a position integration and an unbiased relax over every contact, and the contact softness is formed at the substep width.

rigidRestSpeed.description: Below this speed (world units/second) of its fastest point, the centre's linear speed plus its angular speed times its bounding radius, a supported rigid body counts toward the resting hold window (RigidRestHoldSeconds). It scales with each body's live scale, so a long piece turning slowly about its centre stays awake while its ends still move. Non-negative.

rigidRestHoldSeconds.description: How long a rigid body must stay under the rest speed while supported before the resting latch actually closes — long enough that crossing a contact skin's noise band for one tick never freezes a body mid-roll. Non-negative.

rigidSubstepTravelFraction.description: The fraction of a rigid body's own bounding radius its solved motion may depart from the motion its contact probe certified before a guard sweep re-certifies it against the static field: a smaller fraction guards more often. Strictly positive.

rigidSubstepMinimumTravel.description: The floor (world units) under that departure bound, independent of RigidSubstepTravelFraction — guards a body whose collider is small enough that the fraction alone would derive a near-zero bound. It is also the travel of the support a sleeping body is woken within. Strictly positive.

rigidPairRestitutionSpeed.description: Below this closing speed (world units/second), a rigid contact restitutes at zero rather than its pair's coefficient, so two bodies at rest never micro-bounce. Non-negative; small enough that a real strike is unaffected.

bodyContacts.title: WorldBodyContactPolicy

gridCellSize.description: The world-space cell edge of the distance grid the solid field bakes its program into, so a query far from every surface reads a corner bound instead of marching the program; 0 (the default) bakes no grid and every query reads the exact program. A smaller cell tightens the bound and enlarges the grid. Meaningful only when a requirement selects field contact.
